utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, they inspected this armament at the barracks which housed the 354th Brigade. They verified that brigade, not the command post of the 3rd Army. But they physically placed their vehicle on the concrete surface below which the command post of the 3rd Army was located. Their job, however, was to control the arsenal in the barracks, that is, the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you allowed them to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not that I allowed it. It was not my responsibility to decide whether to allow them to enter or not. That was in keeping with a decision of the command of the Pristina Corps and the brigade commander, and it was also the obligation of our units towards the OSCE team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you understood your obligation was to allow the OSCE access to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you go to paragraph 34, please, where you refer to a group of 60 volunteers, who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are volunteers from the reception centre of the 1st Army that we discussed earlier in my testimony. Those were the ones who displayed lack of discipline in the corps units and they were returned immediately to the reception centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was the nature of the irregular treatment of local inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a group of volunteers who thieved and committed other committed offences against the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I'd like to know what was the nature of the irregular treatment of local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those volunteers went into the houses of the local population without the approval of their superiors, seized property or looted, they treated civilians inappropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I know, a smaller group of volunteers also committed the crimes of murder, that is, a killing of a small group of citizens in the area of Zegra and they were prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that the only area where these people operated or were there other villages affected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, that was the only area where these volunteers committed any crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And lastly, what I'm finding a little difficult to understand is your description of them as one small group of volunteers. This is a group that were working all together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, since I was at the reception centre of the 3rd Army at that time performing my duties as given me by the commander of the 3rd Army receiving volunteers, I am not aware of the details of the criminal acts perpetrated by this group of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did the group have a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they did not have a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, could you tell the Trial Chamber, where is Kursumlija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO KOSTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, Kursumlija is located 60 kilometres from Podujevo on the route Nis-Prokuplje-Podujevo-Pristina so 60 kilometers from Podujevo between Podujevo and Kursumlija is the border between Serbia and Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: So it is in Serbia proper after the -- after you pass the administrative border, outside Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kostic, that completes your evidence; thank you for coming here to give it. You may now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Our gratitude to everyone here for their patience in allowing us to sit a little longer than normal. We shall resume at 2.15 on Thursday.
